newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-ALANIA FACE CRUNCH RUSSIAN LEAGUE TEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALANIA FACE CRUNCH RUSSIAN LEAGUE TEST.

text.p: Alania Vladikavkaz, who have missed three penalties in two successive defeats, face a further test of their Russian league resolve on Saturday.
The 1996 runners-up and 1995 champions, with just three points from three games so far, travel to Samara where Krylya Sovietov (Soviet Wings) are joint top with maximum points.

Alania were hoping for a last-minute reprieve for striker Anatoly Kanishchev, who missed Wednesday's 2-0 home defeat by Zenit after an indefinite league ban imposed when he failed to show up for international duty against Cyprus last weekend.
The disciplinary committee was due to meet late on Friday.

At least Alania, who lost last year's championship in a playoff to Spartak Moscow, will have the services of Georgian sweeper Kakhaber Tskhadadze. A defensive organiser as well as a goalscorer, he missed Wednesday's game through suspension.
Ominously, though, Samara, whose miserly defence earned the curious nickname "The Volga Clothes-pegs" in Soviet days, have yet to concede a goal.
After a 5-0 hammering of KamAZ on the first day of the season, Alania's only real scoring chances in the last two games have been four penalties. They only managed to convert one of them.
Champions and joint leaders Spartak, who humiliated capital rivals Torpedo with three spectacular goals without reply on Wednesday, should have few problems at lowly Tyumen.
